newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kirch's DF1 wins appeal to advertise nationwide.
newsitem.headline: Kirch's DF1 wins appeal to advertise nationwide.

text.p: German digital broadcaster DF1 said on Tuesday it had succesfully appealed against an injunction brought by pay TV station Premiere barring it from advertising its package of channels nationwide.
DF1, which is controlled by media magnate Leo Kirch, said a Hamburg court had suspended an injunction imposed against it barring advertising outside its home state of Bavaria.

The ruling marks the latest twist in the pay TV war between DF1 and Premiere, an analogue package which has won 1.4 million subscribers by offering a mix of Hollywood blockbusters and Bundesliga soccer. DF1 has pulled 20,000 viewers.

Premiere, in which Kirch has a one-quarter stake -- but is at loggerheads with its partners Bertelsmann AG and Canal Plus -- had won the injunction last week by arguing that DF1's licence was only valid in Bavaria.
Both Bertelsmann and French pay TV group Canal Plus want Premiere to be Germany's main digital television outlet, and a pilot project with 30,000 subscribers is planned.

DF1 also said that the Hamburg court had applied for the injunction to be lifted completely. A court spokesman confirmed that the injunction was no longer in force and a further review would be made on Friday.
German news magazines at the weekend reported that Kirch had demanded the dismissal of Premiere managing director Bernd Kundrun.
